summary: The sweep entry 'fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage' carried lineage in its rungId, which no other sweep entry does. rungId names the technique (face-preserving ratio); inputLineage carries the lineage. The promoted row's chosenRungId='fp-r0.4' was correct. The fix renames the sweep entry to 'fp-r0.4' distinguished by inputLineage='tightjeans fit output...', and restores the derived lookup in the test.

rungIdSemanticsInIterateOptimize.note: Rung ids are pure technique names derived from FACE_PRESERVING_RATIOS constants; no lineage suffix anywhere in the source.

sweepEntriesInOtherRows.finding: None of the other four promoted bodies have a 'sweep' array at all. The viseme-inspect row is the only one with a sweep, added by rederive-evidence-drift-2026-09-14.ts to document the two lineages measured. The anomaly was naming one entry with a lineage suffix.

testRatioParse.behavior: Parses 0.4 from 'fp-r0.4'. Would yield NaN on 'fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage', breaking the station run.

chosenRungIdConsumers.behavior: All consumers expect chosenRungId to be a rung id present in the source's ratio list (fp-r0.4, fp-r0.3, fp-r0.15). No consumer expects a lineage suffix.

rejectedOption.reason: Changing chosenRungId to 'fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage' would: (1) break the ratio parse in the test (NaN), requiring a separate fix; (2) break the rung-id counterweight in both test files which validate chosenRungId against the source's FACE_PRESERVING_RATIOS; (3) contradict iterate-optimize.ts where rung ids are pure technique names without lineage; (4) create a precedent where rungId encodes lineage, forcing every future sweep to duplicate rungIds per lineage rather than using inputLineage as designed.

changesMade: docs/openclinxr/humanoid-postopt-ladder-face-preserving-2026-09-11.json: sweep[3].rungId changed from 'fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage' to 'fp-r0.4' (inputLineage unchanged, carries 'tightjeans fit output...')

tools/openclinxr/asset-pipeline/trellis/the-face-preserving-rung-keeps-every-face-triangle.test.ts:176-178: lookup changed from literal 'fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage' to derived entry.rungId === row.chosenRungId && entry.inputLineage?.includes('tightjeans')

verification.expected: All assertions pass; falsifier derives comparison target from report's chosenRungId + inputLineage, not a hardcoded literal

dualSweepEntryHazard.description: Two sweep entries now share rungId 'fp-r0.4' (HB-02 lineage: 68214 tris, tightjeans lineage: 69067 tris). Any consumer doing a bare .find(e => e.rungId === 'fp-r0.4') will silently take the FIRST match (HB-02), which is the wrong body for the promoted row (tightjeans).
dualSweepEntryHazard.currentState: Measured: the test at the-face-preserving-rung-keeps-every-face-triangle.test.ts is currently the ONLY consumer of this sweep array (grep for 'sweep' in tools/openclinxr/asset-pipeline/trellis/*.test.ts returns only that file). The hazard is latent, not live.
dualSweepEntryHazard.mitigation: The test correctly uses the compound key entry.rungId === row.chosenRungId && entry.inputLineage?.includes('tightjeans'). Future consumers must do the same; a bare rungId lookup is insufficient when multiple lineages share a technique.
